morgan: Heads-up — after the new tllm-wrapper refactor (commit 9f7a2b) we see an ~18% E2E latency regression on our TRT/vLLM integration for long sequences (8k). I ran an nsys capture, attaching key snippets below. :eyes:

alex: Ugh. Any quick breakdown from the trace? scheduler vs engine time?

morgan: Short paste from the nsys summary (trimmed):
```
nsys profile run: run_tllm_trt_8k
Total GPU time (kernel only): 452.3 ms
 - TRT engine execute (IExecutionContext::enqueue): 172.1 ms (38%)
 - vLLM scheduler kernels / CPU->GPU sync: 54.2 ms (12%)
 - wrapper memcpy (host->device / device->host): 90.6 ms (20%)
 - per-layer kernels (softmax, gelu, ln): 128.4 ms (28%)
```
Notes: the wrapper memcpy is from the thin layer that packs inputs/outputs for TRT. We used to stream directly into the engine buffers, but wrapper now does an extra host staging copy for safety.

samir: That staging copy rings alarm bells — looks like KV-cache warmup paths might be forcing extra copies per request. Are we pinning the host buffers and using async copies?

morgan: No, current wrapper does plain `malloc` + `cudaMemcpy`. Command I used to repro: `nsys profile -o tllm_trt -t cuda,cudnn --sample=none python -m perf.serve --engine=trt --model=xl-1b --seq_len=8192`

jen: Also saw scheduler overhead: vLLM's scheduler is spinning waiting for batch fill and then doing a synchronous fallback when batch timeout hits. In the trace that shows as small CPU kernels but frequent stream synchronizations — explains the ~12% suspiciously low-level cost. We should move to event-based wakeups (condvar) for the dispatcher and avoid `cudaStreamSynchronize` in the hot path.

alex: Any timeline snippets (nsys timeline / perfetto flame) showing gaps?

morgan: Perfetto capture (uploaded to perfetto.redwood/internal/trace/1763304821) — timeline shows alternating blocks:
 - host serializing / memcpy -> 80-110ms gaps before TRT execute
 - TRT execute bursts around 160-200ms windows
 - small scattered memcpyAsyncs that don't overlap with kernels (streams not lined up)

I pasted the minimal relevant flame excerpt:```
[Host] pack_inputs()      |======= 40ms =======|  |===== 30ms ======|
[Host->GPU memcpy]       |---- 60ms ----|           |----30ms----|
[TRT execute stream 2]   |      ======170ms======|    |===160ms===|
[Scheduler wake / sync]  |--- sync ---|--- sync ---|        |--- sync ---|
```

samir: So two main hotspots: 1) wrapper staging copies blocking overlap, 2) scheduler sync points preventing CUDA overlap. Both are low-effort fixes: preallocate pinned GPU-visible buffers and point TRT IO to them, and switch scheduler to async notifications + queueing.

qa-bot: Repro job 1763304900 completed: baseline (pre-refactor) p95 latency = 412ms, current branch p95 = 486ms.

jen: Another observation: kernel selection in TRT seems to fall back to native GELU implementation on longer sequences (we're seeing cudnn vs custom kernels toggling). The selector heuristic uses sequence length and batch size to pick kernels — maybe the refactor nudged the batch shape distribution so TRT picks slower kernels. We should dump engine profile (`trtexec --dumpLayerInfo`) and compare kernel choices.

alex: Good call. If kernel selection changed, that could explain part of the 28% per-layer delta. Can someone run `trtexec --loadEngine=engine.plan --dumpLayerInfo` on both engines?

morgan: On it. Quick experiment I ran locally: bypassed wrapper memcpy by mapping engine I/O to a preallocated CUDA buffer and using `cudaMemcpyAsync` with pinned staging only for edge cases. Result: p95 dropped from 486ms -> 433ms (~11% improvement), and GPU timeline shows better overlap: wrapper copy time down to 22ms and TRT execute consistent.

samir: Nice. That implies the extra host round-trip was the big offender. Follow-ups:
 - Replace malloc-based staging with pinned host buffers + `cudaMemcpyAsync` -> ensures overlap
 - Ensure TRT engine buffers are persistent across requests to reuse allocations
 - Add telemetry: histogram of memcpy sizes and counts per request to catch regressions automatically

jen: For the scheduler: move to condition-variable based wakeups and avoid `cudaStreamSynchronize` unless in teardown. Also add a soft-batch flush threshold tunable (max_wait_ms) so small tails don't force syncs.

alex: Perf regression root cause summary for postmortem: 
 - primary: wrapper staging copy (extra host-device round trips) -> ~20%
 - secondary: scheduler sync/wake pattern prevents overlap -> ~8%
 - tertiary: kernel selection drift for long seq shapes -> ~~5% (investigating)

morgan: Plan: open PR with pinned-buffer change + scheduler wake refactor + test harness to run nsys in CI on a small sample. I'll include reproducer command and perf artifacts. cc @samir @jen for review.

infra-bot: Job queued: `perf-ci/tllm-trt-smoke/176330` (will run nsys capture and upload artifacts)

jen: Also let's add a short eval to Redwood Console: track average memcpy bytes / request and p95 latency per model+engine to auto-alert when wrapper copy rate spikes.

morgan: Agreed. I'll paste the PR link when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
